items.evidence: From a cold start (no engine running) `python tools/kit.py build` in work/ took about 28 s. It printed a JSON array with name, triangles, closed and bounds for all four: gear_token 320 tris, closed true, x -0.15..0.15, y 0..0.3, z -0.025..0.025; heart 680, true; star 36, true; coin 576, true. The script starts the engine with no window and stops it again.

`python tools/kit.py frames` rewrote frames/gear_token.png, heart.png, star.png and coin.png (new modification times). The PNG headers say 512x512. I opened all four: each is a front view with the whole prop in the frame and a margin all round.

The front frame shows 12 teeth, all alike, with the background showing through a round centre hole. The tooth corner angles in the exported glb repeat every 30 degrees (5.1/24.9, 35.1/54.9, ...: 24 corners). A ray along Z at the centre (0, 0.15) and at r = 0.02 and 0.025 hits nothing, so the hole goes through. My own angled engine frame shows the bore going right through.
The build prints x -0.15..0.15 (0.30 wide), y 0..0.3 (0.30 tall, so it stands on y = 0) and z -0.025..0.025 (0.05 thick). All three are exact.

heart.png shows two round lobes on top with a cleft between them and a point at the bottom. In the frame the edges are visibly bevelled and soft. The glb has z levels +-0.025, +-0.013 and +-0.0043, and rays near the outline get shorter (0.044 to 0.0285 thick), so the rounded edge is a 12 mm, 3-step profile. The point is cut flat about 17 mm wide (see defects), but it still reads as a heart's point.

star.png shows five sharp points. In the glb the five outer vertices are at radius 0.1577 at 18, 90, 162, 234 and 306 degrees, which is 72 degrees apart. Each tip is a single vertex. The build prints x -0.14998..0.14998 (0.30 across) and z -0.025..0.025 (0.05 thick).

The build prints x -0.1..0.1 and y 0..0.2 (0.2 across) and z -0.01..0.01. Rays along Z through the glb give thickness 0.014 (z +-0.007) at r = 0, 0.05 and 0.08, and 0.02 (z +-0.01) at r = 0.09 and 0.095. So the rim is about 0.015 wide and stands 3 mm proud on both faces. An angled engine frame I took shows the raised rim lip.

The build reports closed: true for all four. The script works this out by welding the exported glb and checking that every edge is shared by two triangles, once in each direction. All four recipes take named materials and colours (metal/steel, toy/heart, toy/star, gold/gold) from one assets/style.json palette. They are all flat upright extruded or lathed tokens with the same layout conventions, and in the frames they look like one set.

README gives `python tools/kit.py build` and `python tools/kit.py frames`, to be run from work/. With no engine running, I ran both exactly as written and both succeeded. Each one started the engine and stopped it again.

defects: The heart's bottom point is cut flat about 17 mm wide (outline points +-0.00841 at y = 0), not a true point. The README admits this.
The gear is a dull dark grey (metal/steel) in its frame. That does not fit the style's own 'one bold colour each' description.
Under 'Expected output', the README shows a text table, but the command actually prints JSON. It is a small documentation mismatch.
In the straight-on frame the coin's rim shows only as a faint ring, so the frame alone barely shows the raised rim.
